findings.title: A deserialization call requires trusted input
findings.explanation: Line 7 calls pickle.load(). This loader can reconstruct arbitrary Python objects and invoke code during deserialization. Malicious input could run with this process's privileges. Where the bytes come from has NOT been verified by this detector; trusted internal data and untrusted external data can reach the same call.
findings.fix_hint: Prefer json (or msgpack/cbor) with an explicit schema across trust boundaries; use yaml.safe_load for YAML values. If object serialization is unavoidable, accept only trusted producers and verify an HMAC or digital signature before loading. A checksum supplied alongside untrusted bytes does not authenticate them; a digest helps only when its expected value comes from a trusted source.

findings.title: Environment ignore coverage needs review
findings.explanation: Archive-local ignore coverage was not established for candidate paths: .env. Rules were evaluated for each path, including nested files and negations. Global Git excludes and runtime configuration were not checked. This does not establish that credentials were committed.
findings.fix_hint: For paths used for private configuration, add appropriate ignore rules in their directory or the repository root. Keep intentional public build configuration and templates. Ignore rules do not remove files already tracked by Git.

findings.title: No test files found
findings.explanation: There is nothing that checks your app still works after a change. Right now the only way to find out you broke signup or checkout is a user hitting it in production. That risk grows every time you ask an AI assistant to modify code you are not reading line by line.
findings.fix_hint: Start with one test for the thing that would hurt most if it silently broke — usually payment or login. One test that runs on every change is worth far more than a suite you plan to write later.

findings.title: No Dockerfile found in the archive
findings.explanation: A Dockerfile is one deployment option. Its absence does not establish that the app cannot run on a server; systemd and managed platforms are other options.
findings.fix_hint: Review existing deployment instructions; add a Dockerfile only if containers are needed.

findings.title: No recognized CI configuration found in the archive
findings.explanation: No recognized GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines, Travis, Drone or Buildkite configuration was found. External automation and CI settings outside the archive were not checked.
findings.fix_hint: Check whether external CI already builds and tests this project. If it does not, add a workflow appropriate to the project's build and test commands. Configuration presence alone does not verify successful execution.

A checksum supplied alongside untrusted bytes does not authenticate them; a digest helps only when its expected value comes from a trusted source.

findings.title: Environment ignore coverage needs review
findings.explanation: Archive-local ignore coverage was not established for candidate paths: .env. Rules were evaluated for each path, including nested files and negations. Global Git excludes and runtime configuration were not checked. This does not establish that credentials were committed.
findings.fix_hint: For paths used for private configuration, add appropriate ignore rules in their directory or the repository root. Keep intentional public build configuration and templates. Ignore rules do not remove files already tracked by Git.

findings.title: No test files found
findings.explanation: There is nothing that checks your app still works after a change. Right now the only way to find out you broke signup or checkout is a user hitting it in production. That risk grows every time you ask an AI assistant to modify code you are not reading line by line.
findings.fix_hint: Start with one test for the thing that would hurt most if it silently broke — usually payment or login. One test that runs on every change is worth far more than a suite you plan to write later.

findings.title: No Dockerfile found in the archive
findings.explanation: A Dockerfile is one deployment option. Its absence does not establish that the app cannot run on a server; systemd and managed platforms are other options.
findings.fix_hint: Review existing deployment instructions; add a Dockerfile only if containers are needed.

findings.title: No recognized CI configuration found in the archive
findings.explanation: No recognized GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines, Travis, Drone or Buildkite configuration was found. External automation and CI settings outside the archive were not checked.
findings.fix_hint: Check whether external CI already builds and tests this project. If it does not, add a workflow appropriate to the project's build and test commands. Configuration presence alone does not verify successful execution.
